newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude faces $20 resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude faces $20 resistance.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+NYMEX crude oil faces strong resistance up at $20 a tonne and this is expected ultimately to put downwards pressure on the market.
+First support is seen at $18.85 and then at $18.65 a gallon.
NYMEX crude oil futures face strong resistance at $20 a tonne and this is expected to dampen any possible exuberance, technical analysts said.
"It's quite a mess," said Scott Siller at MCM New York. "It has been pretty choppy but we are still in rally mode."

He saw good resistance up at $20, which is roughly the level of the 30-day and 50-day moving average as well as being an important psychological area. It also corresponded to the 50 percent retracement from the downwards move from the highs of late May/early June to the low point reached this month.
"That $20 area might be a good area of resistance." He also saw another obstacle at $20.30, which corresponds to the 62 percent retracement level from that downwards move.

Underneath the market he saw $18.85 - the low point reached on June 25, as a support level. "If we lose that number it is going to get ugly again and we are going to see a resumption of the weakness."
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International in Gainesvile, Georgia, was more bearish and said the recent $19.75 peak would likely provide a bearish ceiling for the market. But he, too, was cautious.
"Though confidence is not running high, the best guess is that we're headed below $18.65. A break below $18.85 will kick this case into gear

MeesPierson Derivatives in London saw support for gasoline at 55 cents a gallon but were bearish about the August contract. "We would be more likely to join the break through 56.10 on the short side, waiting for 55 or new lows to take profits. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
